chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who had intercourse with his wife while they were both in Ihram. He said: 'If the woman aided with desire along with the desire of the man, then upon them both is the sacrifice (hady), and they are separated from each other until they complete the rituals and until they return to the place where they had intercourse. And if the woman did not aid with desire and her companion compelled her, then there is nothing upon her.'

key_terms.الْمَنَاسِكِ: The rituals of Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الْهَدْيُ: The sacrificial animal (hady) offered as expiation
key_terms.بَاشَرَ: To have sexual intercourse or consummate marriage
key_terms.مُحْرِمَانِ: Both in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a couple having intercourse while both are in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of shared liability in Hajj penalties, distinguishing between mutual consent and unilateral coercion. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the wife's exemption from the sacrificial offering (hady) depends on her lack of active participation in the desire, reinforcing the concept of individual accountability within the marital unit during sacred rites.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Suleyman Bin Khalid, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked himasws about a man who slept with his wife and they were both in Ihraam, ‘What is upon them both?’ So heasws said: ‘If the woman had aided by desire along with the desire of the man, so upon them both would be the sacrifice, together (each), and separation would be effected between the two of them until they are both free from the rituals, and until they both return to the place in which they attained what they attained. And if it was such that the woman did not aid with desire and disliked her companion (doing it), so there is nothing upon her’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is in the state of Ihram as well as his wife and he involves himself in sexual relation with her. He (the Imam) said, ‘If it is with her and his lustfulness, they both owe an offering. They must separate from each other until all acts of al-Hajj are complete and they return to the place where it had happened; if it was not with lust on her part, instead she had despised, then she does not owe anything.’”
